newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali-Malaysian bank opens in Somali capital.
newsitem.headline: Somali-Malaysian bank opens in Somali capital.

text.p: A joint Somali-Malaysian bank opened in the war-ravaged Somali capital of Mogadishu on Friday, offering a connection to the international banking system from isolated Somalia.
The Somali-Malaysian Commercial Bank is backed by a capital investment of $4 million, 70 percent from Malaysian companies and 30 percent from Somali merchants, its Somali director said.
Abdinur Ahmed Darman, a son of a prominent Somali former diplomat, said the Somali-Malaysian bank was registered with foreign banks and could transfer cheques internationally.
The bank's headquarters are in southern Mogadishu in territory which is controlled by faction leader Hussein Aideed.
Darman said the bank was neutral and would have branches in north Mogadishu, Bossaso in the northeast and in Hargeisa, the capital of self-declared Somaliland in the northwest of the country.
In August last year, a Somali telecommunications company opened a money transfer system and bank in Mogadishu, which has had most of its infrastructure destroyed in the civil war.
Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991 and has been divided into a series of rival fiefdoms by clan-based faction leaders.
